text: “ISLAND OF KISSES.

label: text
text:
Film Scenes Being “Shot”
In Hongkong.

label: text
text: A GERMAN COMPANY.

label: text
text: "Director Who Won Fame On" "Quo Vadis."

label: text
text: Few local residents observing three motor cars drawn up outside the Hongkong Hotel this morning just before nine would have associated their occupants with anything more romantic than the ordinary tour of Hongkong by strangers—even if they got that far.

label: text
text: In "fact, these unassuming " tourists" were members of the cost of a film ("The Island of

label: vision_footnote
text: A stirring scene in "Island of Kisses," taken in Jamaica, depicting a thrilling rescue of the heroine by the hevo.

label: text
text: Kisses") in which the settings of Hongkong play a part and which Hongkong will doubtless have the opportunity of witnessing some time after its release in December.

label: text
text: The director of the Company is Mr. George Jacoby, who won fame by his work on "Quo Vadis," a picture which was successfully shown in Hongkong recently. Conversing with a "China Mail" representative this morning, he stated that he entered into the contract by which the rights of the pictures on which he is now engaged were secured by Universal Pictures Corporation, before the tour began and although the costs incurred were naturally very high he hoped to make the tour a successful one financially. It is the first world tour of its kind (for securing settings in all parts of the world) which has been undertaken since the war.

label: text
text: There are some distinguished actors and actresses taking part in these films (the other is "The Woman Without a Name"). Dr. A. Schirokauer, who travels with them, is turning his broad experience of authorship to the task of adapting scenarios, as need arises, to the conditions in different ports; George Alexander, who starred in "Love Is Blipd" is in the cast, also Jack Trevor and Stuart Rome, a well-known English actor. The lady "stars" are Elga Brink, the "Mary Pickford of Germany," and Marietta Millner, a Vienna girl who whilst the company was in Hollywood, accepted a contract made her by Famous Players.

label: text
text:
An "Ideal Place."
In converse with the director and some of the members of the cast this morning, the “China Mail” gathered that Hongkong was considered one of the most ideal places for the shooting of the type of film on which they are engaged. The company will remain here for six days—“all too short for what we would like to get through,” said Mr. Jacoby,—and in view of the possibilities offering film directors here and in Shanghai it is probable that a scenario will be specially written round the two places, plans having been made for the company to return here next year to screen the action in a typical “Paris of the Orient” setting. The scenario is to depict the struggle of a young American who, sent to the Far East on a business trip, falls in love with a Chinese girl, eomplications resulting from the antagonism of the parents of both of the youthful couple.

label: text
text: The “Island of Kisses,” on the shooting of scenes in which the Company is engaged today (scenes are being taken in the Chinese quarter, the European quarter and even up the Peak I) is the tale of a romantic orphan maiden who starts out nearly penniless to see the world and after various hair-breadth escapes is overtaken and rescued by her

label: paragraph_title
text: WUCHANG'S FATE.

label: text
text: CITY NOT YET TAKEN BY CANTON

label: text
text: BOTH SIDES' CLAIMS.

label: text
text: As is usual when something important is at stake in Chinese warfare, the opposing sides make claims which are greatly at variance.

label: text
text: Canton broadcasted on Sunday a despatch that Wuchang had been taken, that Wu Pei-fu's bodyguards had looted the Bank of China and Communications Bank in Hankow, and that he had fled on a Yangtze gunboat. On Monday, the anti-Canton section of the press was reticent.

label: text
text: Since then it has been established that although the situation is critical for the northerners, the stronghold of Wuchang has not fallen.

label: text
text: It is conceded that the northerners were still falling back. At the most they could only have held their line in places.

label: text
text: The southern Nationalists are pushing forwards steadily and may yet take Wuchang, the fall of which will mean the end of Wu Pei-fu's tenure in Hankow.

label: text
text: But a local merchant received only yesterday a cable from an agent in Hankow, asking him to hurry up shipments of sugar from Hongkong as the market was likely to go up.

label: text
text: An anti-Canton source hints that the present acting Premier in Peking has ordered the Chinese Navy in Fukien to attack Swatow. It is generally accepted that Marshal Sun Chuan-fang, who is Wu Pei-fu's ally in Shanghai and hinterland, has not taken the field on either side.

label: text
text: Reinforcements are being rushed southwards by Wu Pei-fu and a stand on the banks of the Yangtze River may be made with good effect.

label: text
text: The odds, at present, are still n Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER.

label: text
text: The Observatory report at 11.10 a.m. to-day states that pressure has increased moderately over N.E. China and slightly from E. China to S.W. Japan and Formosa. It is "nearly stationary elsewhere. A trough of relatively low pressure extends from Indo-China to Yap. An anticyclone has formed over N.E. China. A moderate, temporary, N.E. monsoon may be expected along the coast of China.

label: text
text: Until noon tomorrow the weather forecast is east winds, moderate; fair.

label: text
text: "The Woman without a Name," upon which the company will engage on later in the course of their stay in Hongkong, follows the adventures of a woman editor who as a publicity device, disappears from New York, offering a huge reward to anyone who finds her within three months. A rival editor, masculine, accepts the "challenge" but is won by romance from capitalising his success.

label: text
text: Whilst engaged in making screen drama on the Whangpoo near the Dollar Wharf in Shanghai last Thursday, the members of the Company suddenly found themselves acting in real drama. Their little fleet of junks and launches was first to the rescue when a big English cargo boat ran down a Chinese junk, capsized it, cut it in two, and flung fifteen people into the river.

label: text
text:
Before the steamer could put out its boat, the actors were playing hero in real earnest and had saved all the victims, including a lad of twelve who was imprisoned, screaming, in the upturned hulk so that his rescuers had to cut their way through to him.
Resourcefulness may well be the characteristic of this company who have been out since May on a six months' trip round the world. So far they have touched Belgium, Holland, New York, Panama, Cuba, New Orleans, the Apache Trail, Hollywood, Honolulu, Japan and Shanghai. They leave Hongkong later on the "Macedonia" for Colombo and will also work at Cairo and Naples before returning to Berlin.

text: Pola Negri, in a most tearful condition and accompanied by a doctor and nurse, was prominent among the film celebrities crowding St. Malachi's Church at the Requiem Mass for Rudolph Valentino.

text: The coffin was carried two miles through crowded main streets and later borne back to the mortuary, where it will remain until a burial place is selected.

label: paragraph_title
text: "FLOWERY" APPEALS BY TENANTS.

label: text
text: AlLEGED INCREASES.

label: text
text:
"Flowery" language is used profusely by two of the correspondents to the "China Mail" on the subject of rent increases in the Colony.
One emphasises "secrecy" over a schedule he has prepared "for fear of reprisals" by his 'heartless' landlord.

label: text
text: Tenants—both Chinese and foreign—are invited to write to the "China Mail," giving particulars of rentals having been raised since the Restriction Ordinance lapsed on July 1.

label: text
text: A foreigner, who does not wish his "cuse" to be published, says that his rent, for a house in a "central locality," used both as offices and residence, with the basement as godown, has been the subject of a notice by the owner's solicitor. He is warned that he must vacate by a certain date, after which possession can only be maintained at a figure which works out at 70 per cent, more than the former rental.

label: text
text: A grocer at Queen's Road East, No. 158, alleges that his rent has been increased from $60 to $100 per month. After a reference to the decreased turnover, he prays that the Editor will see to it that his rent is again at the old figure for which his gratitude will know no bounds! He concludes with an enjoinder that business must be preserved by keeping rents down.

label: text
text: Other Chinese correspondents refer to the influence of the "strike" on trade.

label: text
text: The occupant of a tenement flat at West Point, in a row of about 20 houses, tells how an increase of $24 (on $46) was cut down by $10 to $14, after negotiation and “remonstration” with the landlord. He particularly requests that detail be not published as that $10 may be put on again.

label: text
text:
Bank's Property.
From Staunton Street, a tenant of a flat gives figures which may mean either an increase of $6 or $20. The omission of certain words —whether by intention or accident—makes his letter exceedingly vague. The owners are a local native bank. A phrase the writer uses is rather unique. Broadly translated, it reads:—I therefore respectfully request the gentlemen of your esteemed paper to give prominence to report by early publication.

label: text
text: Chinese correspondents should not be dealt with as they have little value. Where a request is stated, details will not be put in print. In no case will they be divulged.

text: [To the Editor of the "China Mail"]

label: text
text: Sir,—I do not know if the following will interest you as being another aspect of the rents poser, but if it does you are at liberty to publish same if you please.

label: text
text: I took a flat in the western district 15 years ago.

label: paragraph_title
text: TENANT SUCCEEDS.

label: text
text:
LANDLORD NOT FULFILLED
COVENANT.

label: text
text: GAS FITTINGS CASE.

label: text
text: Judgment was given for Mons Albert (proprietor of the Albert Cafe) in the Summary Court this morning in both claims and counterclaim in a case in which he was sued by his Chinese landlord for rent in respect of No. 6 Kennedy Road.

label: text
text:
His Honour (Mr. Justice Wood) held that the landlord's claim could not succeed. There had been a conflict of evidence as to the consideration in respect of which a receipt for rent was given. It was not necessary for him in dismissing the claim with costs, said His Honour, to decide what was in fact the consideration accepted on the landlord's behalf.
His Honour found that when possession was given under the agreement, the covenant had not been fulfilled. His Honour also found that the expenditure by the defendant in making up this deficiency was reasonable. With regard to the claim of the landlord that certain fittings for which he was liable had been put in by the tenant without consulting him, His Honour found that this argument had no weight. Notice by the tenant which was necessary to create a breach by the landlord of a covenant to repair was not necessary to create a breach of a covenant which was to supply gas fittings at the commencement of the tenancy at a time when the landlord had full knowledge of his landlord.

label: text
text: The only obstacle to the success of the counterclaim by the defendant was the evidence of the landlord that compensation for this breach of covenant had already been given by the credit allowed of the sum expended in the account for rent. If the tenant's story was to be accepted he had not in fact received this compensation. The onus of proof lay with the landlord on this issue of fact and His Honour found that this had not been discharged in that he had not convinced His Honour that such compensation had been made.

label: text
text:
In giving judgment for the defendant on claim and counterclaim, His Honour said that he had no reason to question the bona fides of the landlord's aims.
Mr. W. B. Hind appeared for plaintiff and Mr. L. D. Turner for the defence.

label: paragraph_title
text: THREE ROWDIES.

label: paragraph_title
text: SQUABBLE IN EUROPEAN HOUSEHOLD.

label: text
text: SERVANTS BOUND OVER.

label: text
text: Three servants employed at No. 3, The Albany, were brought before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy for disorderly conduct.

label: text
text: The first defendant, a house boy in the employ of Mr. E. R. Dovey, said that he was putting on his shoes when the second defendant, a coolie also employed there, flung a bottle at him which injured his hand whilst attempting to shield his face.

label: text
text: The second defendant alleged that he was assaulted without any provocation by the first defendant, who enlisted the aid of two other servants.

label: text
text: No questions were put to the third defendant, Mr. Grantham's servant.

label: text
text: Mr. Dovey, who was present in court, thought there had apparently been bad feeling between the servants as to who had been the informer in a recent raid carried out by the police in the servants' quarters.

label: text
text: All the defendants were bound over on personal bonds of $50 to keep the peace for six months.

label: text
text: A Chinese youth was fined $5 at the Central Magistracy this morning for indulging in the dangerous practice of carrying a companion almost perched on the handle bar of a cycle. The youth was caught by a Shantung constable at Connaught Road Central shortly after 10 p.m.
